=== PR 11 BODY ===
# PR 11: Review visibility and run inputs (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY slices A, B, C)

## Summary

Implements `docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md` and its three slice PRDs in one change set (branch `feature-ultra`, worktree `md-manager-ultra`). Handoff with evidence: `docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md`.

- **Slice A – reviewer as an attachable native session.** The review node launches `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer` in `review-worktree/` with Read, Glob, Grep and exactly one allowed write (`review.completion.json` via `--allowedTools "Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)"` under `dontAsk`), attaches a third `Claude: reviewer` Herdr pane, waits for the completion file bound to run, launch token, bundle hash and candidate, re-checks identity/independence/worktree/evidence, writes `review.json` for every verdict and stops the session with the identity re-check. Interrupts leave the reviewer running and resume; the deadline stops it; nothing ever relaunches. `--reviewer-transport print` keeps the headless fallback. New `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`.
- **Slice B – review results in the viewer.** Projects contract 1.2.0 adds `reviewResult` (`.../reviews/{attempt}`); export 1.2.0 adds the `review` section; `workflow export <run>` re-exports old runs; the adapter serves the verdict, findings and `review.diff` as a hash-checked artifact; the review node shows verdict, reviewer, bundle link, summary line, findings grouped by disposition or worker, and the diff link.
- **Slice C – run inputs.** `runInputs` (`.../inputs`) from plan, policy and receipts; Assignment tab and worker-node Task / Exact prompt / Launch receipt / Reported-by-worker / Handoff / Stop panels; finding quotes link to the worker task scrolled to the highlighted quote (verbatim matching only; measured 8/8 live).
- Feature directories `features/review-result/` and `features/run-inputs/` plus `launch` choices, RUNBOOK and README updates.

## Verification

- Python controller: 124 tests (59 before); backend: 30; contracts: 13; unit: 130; browser: 15 scenarios in each of the worker and candidate phases; build, lint and `git diff --check` clean.
- Live smoke test (PRD slice A §5) on a scratch copy of project-workflows-001's bundle: four reviewer sessions exercised the launch defects (variadic option order, `Edit(//path)` rule family), the deadline path, the fail-closed rejection (reviewer invented severity `P3`) and the full accept path.
- Adversarial audit (six lenses) found fourteen defects, all fixed with tests (see handoff §2/§6).
- Re-export of a copy of project-workflows-001 shows its verdict, reviewer dd7bdcd1, six findings and inputs through the real adapter with no absolute paths. The live run directory was not modified.

## After merge

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m workflow export ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001
```

Re-exports the first run so the viewer shows its review and inputs (the `main` adapter only accepts export 1.0.0 until then).

     2	
     3	Status: Draft for approval — implementation has not started. Umbrella: [PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md](PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md). Ordered after slice A by choice, so this run's own review exercises the reviewer pane live. Displaying persisted review results does not technically require A; the only coupling is that findings' `worker` and `requirement` fields are defined by A's completion schema, and the contract treats both as optional so runs reviewed before A still export.
     4	
     5	## 1. Goal
     6	
     7	The review node in the Projects viewer shows the verdict, the reviewer session, the bundle hash it reviewed, and every finding with severity and disposition. After this slice merges, project-workflows-001 shows its own six findings.
     8

=== PR 9 handoff ===
     1	# Slice A handoff — Reviewer as an attachable native session
     2	
     3	Implements [PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md](PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md) (slice A of [PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md](PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md)) on top of `61e4752`. Controller, completion schema and docs only: no `server/` or `src/` change, so slices B and C are untouched and still need their own feature runs.
     4	
     5	Environment: this worktree has no `node_modules` or `.venv`; commands below ran with `ln -s ../md-manager/node_modules node_modules` and the main checkout's interpreter (`../md-manager/.venv/bin/python`), which is what the repository's own `.venv/bin/python` would be.
     6	
     7	Baseline before the change: **70 Python tests, 10 contract tests**, both green. After: **94 Python tests, 13 contract tests**, `npx tsc -b` and `npx eslint .` clean.
     8	
     9	## What changed
    10	
    11	| Area | Change |
    12	|---|---|
    13	| `contracts/workflow/v1.ts`, `examples.ts`, `reviewCompletion.schema.json` | New `reviewCompletion` message plus `validateReviewCompletion`; findings carry `worker` and `requirement` |
    14	| `workflow/sessions.py` | `REVIEWER` node id and `file_prefix`, so the reviewer's files are `review.*` |
    15	| `workflow/interactive.py` | `worktree()`/`receipt_path()` generalise the worker identity checks; `run_reviewer()` launches `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer`; `attach_reviewer_pane()` adds the third pane; `attach-one --node reviewer` |
    16	| `workflow/automatic.py` | `reviewer_transport` run setting; `wait_review`, `read_review_completion`, `native_review`, `print_review`, `resumable_review` |
    17	| `workflow/pipeline.py` | `launch_reviewer` (receipt, events, pane), `stop_session`/`stop_reviewer`, findings with `worker`/`requirement` accepted |
    18	| `workflow/launch.py` | `--reviewer-transport` pinned into `prepare` |
    19	| Docs | RUNBOOK reviewer-session section and recovery entry, feature README "The reviewer pane", contract README, INTERACTIVE_SESSIONS, VALIDATION |
    20	
    21	## Increment 1 — The completion contract
    22	
    23	| Step | Command | Observed |
    24	|---|---|---|
    25	| Red | `npm run test:contracts` (new negative cases, before `v1.ts`) | `validateReviewCompletion is not a function`; the schema-drift test also failed because `reviewCompletion.schema.json` did not exist. |
    26	| Green | `npm run contracts:export && npm run test:contracts` | **13 passed**. Covers the run/bundle/candidate bindings, an unknown field, a finding without `worker`, an empty requirement quote, a blocked verdict with no findings and an approval over an open P1. |
    27	
    28	## Increment 2 — The reviewer session and its wait
    29	
    30	| Step | Command | Observed |
    31	|---|---|---|
    32	| Red | `.venv/bin/python -m unittest workflow.test_automatic` (after the transport default flipped to native, before the controller work) | **3 errors, 1 failure**. `AttributeError: 'FakeSessions' object has no attribute 'run_reviewer'`, and the resumed controller processes exited 1 with `RuntimeError: Non-retryable graph failure`. This is the real signal that the graph now takes the native path. |
    33	| Green | same command | **31 passed** in that module. |
    34	
    35	Behaviour covered: a bound completion file with `worker`/`requirement`; foreign run id, launch token, bundle hash or candidate rejected; schema violations rejected; a blocked verdict with no findings and an approval over an unresolved P1 rejected; a symlinked or oversized file never read; an idle reviewer with no file timing out; a completion written while the session is still `working` not accepted; a missing or blocked session stopping rather than relaunching.
    36	
    37	## Increment 3 — Pane, stop and interrupted-review resume
    38	
    39	| Step | Command | Observed |
    40	|---|---|---|
    41	| Green | `.venv/bin/python -m unittest workflow.test_interactive` | **17 passed**: the launch command's tools (`Read,Glob,Grep,Write`, no Bash, no `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), `--permission-mode dontAsk`, `--add-dir <run>`, the candidate worktree as cwd, reconciliation without relaunch, a dirty worktree refused, the third pane in the workers' tab, its `attach-one --node reviewer` command, its idempotence, and the two refusals (no tab, unverified session). |
    42	| Green | `.venv/bin/python -m unittest workflow.test_pipeline` | **11 passed**, including the reviewer stop: identity-checked, idempotent, recorded as `review/stopped`, and blocked when the stop fails or termination is unproven. |
    43	| Green | `.venv/bin/python -m unittest workflow.test_automatic.AutomaticGraphTests.test_recovery_in_actual_new_controller_processes` | Four real controller processes, exit codes `[75, 130, 75, 0]`: the third step is interrupted mid-review, the reviewer receipt survives, `automatic-review.json` stays `running`, no `review.stop.json` is written, and the next process re-enters the same session (same launch token, same reviewer in `review.json`) without launching a second reviewer. |
    44	
    45	### Mutation checks (the tests fail when the behaviour is removed)
    46	
    47	| Removed | Result |
    48	|---|---|
    49	| The run/token/bundle/candidate binding in `read_review_completion` | `ReviewCompletionTests` → `AssertionError: ValueError not raised` |
    50	| The `REVIEWER in mapping` early return in `attach_reviewer_pane` | pane test → `AssertionError: 8 != 4` (a second pane allocated) |
    51	| The `failures == ["review"]` branch in `advance_failed_checks` | `test_only_an_interrupted_review_of_a_live_session_resumes` → failed; the four-process test still passed, because LangGraph records no task error for a `KeyboardInterrupt`. The branch is the guard for a review failure that *is* recorded, and it is now tested directly rather than only by that path. |
    52	
    53	## Decisions and deviations worth knowing
    54	
    55	- **Reviewer tools are `Read,Glob,Grep,Write`, not read-only.** The PRD asks for both read-only tools and a reviewer-written completion file; those are incompatible. Write is the minimum that makes the protocol work. The containment is elsewhere: no Bash, no agents, no MCP servers, and before any verdict is accepted the reviewer's worktree must still be the clean candidate commit and the bundle and diff hashes must be unchanged. `InteractiveSessions.reviewer_tools` and `reviewer_permission_mode` are single constants if the live smoke test shows `dontAsk` refuses that write; the fallback would be `--add-dir` plus a bypass mode.
    56	- **Third pane in the same tab**, as proposed in the PRD and confirmed by the operator. It is created when the review node starts, not at `start`, so it is `attach_reviewer_pane`, not `attach_panels`. A run with no Herdr tab records `review/detached` and continues unattended.
    57	- **`reviewer_transport` is pinned into `plan.json`** by `prepare`, like the deadlines, so a resumed controller cannot change transport mid-run. Plans prepared before this slice have no key and default to `native`.
    58	- **A deadline does not stop the reviewer.** Workers are stopped when their deadline expires because they keep consuming usage; an idle reviewer does not, and stopping it is left to the operator, as for any unfinished session.
    59	- Findings keep `worker` and `requirement` optional in `Pipeline.validate_review`, so `project-workflows-001`'s existing `review.json` still validates.
    60	
    61	## Not done
    62	
    63	- **The controlled live smoke test (PRD section 5) has not been run.** Nothing here has talked to a real Claude session: the pane, the `--bg` launch, `dontAsk` plus a write into an `--add-dir` path, and a real model's compliance with the completion protocol are all still unproven. That test is the gate the PRD sets before merging, and it needs an operator in Herdr.
    64	- Slice A's second open question (failing earlier than the timeout when a session is idle with no file) is left open for workers and reviewer together, as the PRD asks.

=== PR 10 handoff ===
     1	# Handoff: review visibility (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY, slices A, B pre-run, C pre-run)
     2	
     3	Date: 2026-09-21. Branch `feature-high`, worktree `~/dev/md-manager-high`. Committed as one change on 2026-09-22; the file groups under "Suggested commits" describe how it splits by slice. No feature run was launched.
     4	
     5	## What was built
     6	
     7	### Slice A: reviewer as an attachable native session (complete)

     9	Controller + completion schema + docs, as the PRD scopes it.
    10	
    11	- `contracts/workflow/v1.ts`, `examples.ts`, `contract.test.ts`, generated `reviewCompletion.schema.json`: the completion-file schema. Findings require `worker` (`ui|adapter|both|none`) and `requirement` (verbatim quote or null).
    12	- `workflow/interactive.py`: `SESSION_NODES` adds `review`; `worktree_of`, `reconcile`, `launch` and `run_reviewer` generalise the native launcher.     68	- Reviewer tools: Read, Glob, Grep plus Write of exactly one path (the completion file); the PRD's "Read, Glob, Grep only" cannot produce a file, so the single allowed write is the minimal deviation and is documented in the RUNBOOK.
    69	- An `approved` verdict carrying an unresolved P0/P1 is recorded as `verdict: "blocked"` in `review.json` (the reviewer's raw decision is kept in `automatic-review.json`), so every persisted review satisfies the contract's cross-field rule.

Recorded in the PRD table and the umbrella decisions log.

    """Rebuild `run-state.json` under the current export version from persisted run files.

    exported with a fabricated section.

    from types import SimpleNamespace
    directory = directory.resolve()
    plan = read_json(directory / "plan.json")
    if "automatic" in plan:

        validate_automatic(plan)
    if set(plan.get("nodes", {})) != set(NODES) or not plan.get("base_commit"):

    policy = validate_pipeline_policy(read_json(directory / "policy.json"))

        raise ValueError("Pinned policy changed")
    runtime = SimpleNamespace(directory=directory, plan=plan, policy=policy)
    review_path = directory / "review.json"

def read_review_completion(runtime, bundle: dict, digest: str, token: str) -> dict:
    """Schema plus the bindings the schema cannot express. Validity is not acceptance."""
    from .verification import validate_schema
    path = runtime.directory / "review.completion.json"
    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size > 65536:
        raise ValueError("Invalid reviewer completion file")
    item = read_json(path)
    validate_schema("reviewCompletion", item)
    if (item["run_id"] != runtime.plan["run_id"] or item["launch_token"] != token
            or item["bundle_sha256"] != digest or item["candidate_commit"] != bundle["candidate_commit"]):
        raise ValueError("Stale or foreign reviewer completion signal")
    # Cross-field rules mirrored from contracts/workflow/v1.ts.
    if item["verdict"] == "blocked" and not item["findings"]:
        raise ValueError("A blocked verdict must name the findings that caused it")
    if item["verdict"] == "approved" and any(finding["severity"] != "P2" and finding["disposition"] != "resolved"
                                             for finding in item["findings"]):
        raise ValueError("Approval cannot leave an unresolved P0/P1 finding")
    return {"verdict": item["verdict"], "findings": item["findings"]}

findings.title: 'Rewarded twice, penalised once' is arithmetically void under a mean; the deviation's net effect is one process penalty
findings.detail: PR 11's six code dims other than adapter and ui sum to 49.9 (mean 8.32). Adding adapter 8.5 and ui 8 gives 66.4/8 = 8.30. The extra dims therefore add nothing to its code-quality mean; the only net effect of implementing B and C directly is the spec-fidelity high inside its 6.3 process mean. That is a single, correctly placed penalty, and it is the reason PR 11 loses 'better job' at equal weight despite winning code quality. The deviation itself is confirmed: the branch commit 61e4752 is the one that tightened slice A and set the A-then-runs order, and PR 11 rewrote the umbrella status to record the choice.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic from the gap's figures: 66.4 - 8.5 - 8 = 49.9; 49.9/6 = 8.32; 66.4/8 = 8.30. `git log`: 61e4752 `Tighten slice A scope and clarify slice ordering in the review PRDs`. PR 11 PRD diff on docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md: `+All three were implemented directly in one change set rather than as two feature runs.`; docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:21 (main) `each run has a smaller, focused diff and a blocked run loses one slice, not all three`. findings.title: Only PR 10 single-sources the completion schema; PR 11 deserves the same triplication note PR 9 got
findings.detail: Resolves the fairness contradiction. PR 10 defines reviewCompletion in v1.ts, generates the JSON with contracts:export, and has the Python controller load that JSON for both native validation and print-mode structured output. PR 9 has a generated JSON plus a hand-rolled Python REVIEW_FINDING/REVIEW_SCHEMA for print mode. PR 11 has neither a v1.ts definition nor a contract test: a hand-written JSON (its README says so) plus the same hand-rolled Python dict. So contracts-and-schemas' low on PR 9 applies at least equally to PR 11, and PR 11's medium for breaking the v1.ts-is-authoritative rule stands (spec-fidelity's downgrade to low citing verification.schema.json ignores that the README rule and the contract test both exist and PR 11 used neither).

toolu_016ugad1vqipGzb4Rn9m4RvL.summary: I investigated the aggregation gap rather than re-scoring dimensions: I reconstructed per-PR sums from the verifier means quoted in the gap (the full per-dimension table is not on disk; only the aggregates, PR 9's adapter 0 / ui 1 / export 6 and PR 11's adapter 8.5 / ui 8 are known), read the umbrella and slice PRDs on main to establish which surfaces slice A was told not to touch, and verified in code every fact the disputed scores rest on (adapter version gate, the status-to-export rewrite path, plan-schema strictness, schema provenance, reviewer launch flags). Code quality is PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 under every convention I tried (PR 11 8.3, PR 10 between 7.1 and 8.2 depending on its two unknown N/A-surface scores, PR 9 4.9). But once one N/A convention (exclude dimensions where a PR shipped nothing by design) is applied consistently and the two questions are separated with equal weight, "did the better job" most likely flips to PR 10 > PR 11 > PR 9 (about 7.7 vs 7.3 vs 5.5); PR 11 wins that question only if code quality is weighted at 65% or more of "the job". So the gap changes the second answer and PR 9's score (4.4 to 5.5), not the code-quality ranking. Along the way I resolved the export-bump contradiction as HIGH for PR 10 (a routine `workflow status` on the historic run rewrites it at 1.2.0 and main's adapter then 500s the entire workflow list), confirmed PR 9's compat score is earned rather than "by omission", and found that the "PR 11 rewarded twice" concern is arithmetically void under a mean (adding 8.5 and 8 to six dims averaging 8.32 yields 8.30).
toolu_016ugad1vqipGzb4Rn9m4RvL.pr9: Code quality 4.9 (six applicable code dims; adapter-server and ui-and-browser-tests excluded as by-design N/A per docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:17 and docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:5; export-and-compat stays in and is genuinely earned because main's planSchema is a non-strict z.object (server/projects.ts:84) so the new reviewer_transport key is harmless and export_state.py:38 keeps "1.0.0"). Process 6.0. Overall (equal weight) 5.5, up from the raw 4.4, but still last on both questions for a substantive reason, not an N/A artefact: the launch at md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185,219-220 passes `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk` with no `--allowedTools` rule, which PR 10 (handoff line 59-60) and PR 11 (handoff line 54-55) both observed live is denied, so the default native transport cannot produce a verdict; PR 9 skipped the smoke test the PRD makes the merge gate (PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60) and says so honestly (body item 2). Its attach_panels also never adds the third pane (only attach_reviewer_pane does), against work item 3's wording. Cleanest scope discipline and the tightest diff of the three, but a non-working feature.
toolu_016ugad1vqipGzb4Rn9m4RvL.pr10: Code quality between 7.1 and 8.2 depending on the two verifier scores it received for adapter-server and ui (unknown to me; it shipped no server/ or src/ file, so under the exclude convention both drop out and its six real code dims average (50.4 - a - u)/6); my point estimate is 7.4. Process 8.0, the best of the three: it did exactly the slice A the PRDs describe, proved it live twice with artifacts on disk (~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001/ contains review.completion.json, review.json, review.stop.json, review.interactive.json), and its "extra" work is the B PRD's own pre-run list (PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md:11-19). Overall (equal weight) about 7.7. Its one real code defect is HIGH and I verified the mechanism end to end: `workflow status <run>` reaches `print(f"Report: {report(runtime, state)}")` (md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:688), report() calls export_state (479-481), which writes EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0" (export_state.py:16); main's adapter still has `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` with '1.0.0' (server/projects.ts:37,52), listRuns (320-346) has try/finally with no catch, and projectRun throws invalidRun -> 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID (420-421). One status on project-workflows-001 hides the whole workflow list, and the handoff (line 77) understates this as "that run's listing". It is a narrow, fixable defect that the PRD's own plan half-creates, and it is already priced into its export-and-compat score. PR 10 is also the only PR with a single-sourced completion schema (v1.ts -> generated JSON -> completion_schema() at automatic.py:129-131).
toolu_016ugad1vqipGzb4Rn9m4RvL.pr11: Code quality 8.3 (all eight code dims apply; it wrote adapter and UI code and it is good). Process 6.3, dragged by a confirmed high: it implemented B and C directly in one 56-file, +6074 commit after the user had, in the very commit it branched from (61e4752 "Tighten slice A scope and clarify slice ordering"), split the work so that "each run has a smaller, focused diff and a blocked run loses one slice, not all three" (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:21), and it rewrote the umbrella PRD's status to say so (its own PRD diff). Overall (equal weight) 7.3. The critic's worry that it is "rewarded twice" for the deviation does not survive arithmetic: its other six code dims average 8.32 and adding 8.5 and 8 moves the mean to 8.30, so under a mean the only net effect of the deviation is the spec-fidelity penalty. It is the only PR under which the existing run keeps loading after re-export or `status` (server/projects.ts:44 EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']; test_export.py:185; projects.test.ts:1049), it caught the variadic --add-dir ordering bug (interactive.py:220-226), and it ran four live sessions. Against that, it hand-writes reviewCompletion.schema.json (contracts/workflow/README.md:12 admits "hand-written, not generated from v1.ts"), adds no contract test for it, and duplicates the shape again in Python (automatic.py:129-141), the same triplication contracts-and-schemas faulted PR 9 for.
toolu_016ugad1vqipGzb4Rn9m4RvL.ranking_reason: This is the "did the better job" ranking under one stated rule: exclude a dimension for a PR that shipped nothing on that surface by design (adapter-server and ui for PR 9 and PR 10; export-and-compat stays for everyone), score each fact once (the PR 10 version mismatch lives in export-and-compat only), then average code-quality and process equally. Under that rule PR 10 scores about 7.7, PR 11 7.3 and PR 9 5.5; PR 10 beats PR 11 for any value of its two unknown N/A-surface scores summing below 10.6, which is near-certain given PR 9 received 0 and 1 on the same two dims for the same reason. Substantively: PR 10 did the slice the user scoped hours earlier, proved it live, and its one high (status rewrites the historic run at 1.2.0 and the whole workflow list 500s) is narrow and fixable; PR 11 has the best code and the most complete feature but did a different, larger job than the one specified, in the single big commit the plan was written to avoid; PR 9 is last on both questions because its native reviewer cannot write the completion file and it skipped the gate that would have shown that. The code-quality ranking is different and robust: PR 11 (8.3) > PR 10 (7.1-8.2) > PR 9 (4.9). PR 11 takes "better job" too only if the person weights code quality at 65% or more of the job; the raw 11-dimension means (7.8 / 6.7 / 4.4) hide that flip because they score PR 9 and PR 10 at or near zero on surfaces the PRD told them not to touch.

findings.title: Three N/A conventions (0, 1, 6) are inconsistent; adopt exclude, and export-and-compat is not N/A for PR 9
findings.detail: Dimensions where a PR shipped nothing by design should be excluded from that PR's mean, not scored 0 (adapter-server), 1 (ui) or 6 (export). The umbrella PRD assigns slice A to `workflow/` + `contracts/workflow/` + docs and defers server/ and src/ to feature runs, and the diffstats confirm PR 9 and PR 10 touch neither directory. export-and-compat is different: PR 9's plan.json gains `reviewer_transport`, which is input to the adapter, so the dimension applies and PR 9's 6 is earned (main's planSchema is a non-strict z.object and zod 4.6.5 strips unknown keys; export_state.py stays at 1.0.0). Recomputed: PR 9 all-11 4.4 -> 9-dim 5.3; excluding export as well would wrongly give 5.2.

findings.title: Separating 'code quality' from 'better job' with a consistent N/A rule most likely flips the second answer to PR 10
findings.detail: Code-only means with N/A excluded: PR 9 29.4/6 = 4.9; PR 11 66.4/8 = 8.3; PR 10 = (50.4 - a - u)/6 where a,u are its adapter/ui verifier scores (not on disk). PR 11 keeps the code lead unless a+u < 0.5. Process means: 6.0 / 8.0 / 6.3. 'Better job' at equal weight: PR 9 5.45, PR 11 7.32, PR 10 = ((50.4-a-u)/6 + 8)/2, which exceeds PR 11 whenever a+u < 10.6. PR 9 received 0 and 1 on those two dims for the identical reason (nothing shipped there), so PR 10's are almost certainly well under 10.6; at a+u = 6 PR 10 is 7.7. PR 11 wins 'better job' only if code weight w satisfies 8.3w + 6.33(1-w) > 7.4w + 8.0(1-w), i.e. w > 0.65. The raw 11-dim means (7.8/6.7/4.4) hide this because they score two PRs near zero on surfaces the PRD told them not to touch.
findings.evidence: Inputs are the verifier aggregates quoted in the gap: raw 11-dim 4.4/6.7/7.8; code-only 3.8 (4.9 sans N/A)/6.3/8.3; process 6.0/8.0/6.3; PR 9 adapter 0, ui 1, export 6; PR 11 adapter 8.5, ui 8. Reconstructed sums: PR 9 code 30.4, process 18.0; PR 10 code 50.4, process 24.0; PR 11 code 66.4 (six non-adapter/ui dims sum 49.9), process 19.0. No verifier score file exists under the scratchpad (`ls` and `grep -rl verifier` returned only diffs and run copies).

findings.title: `workflow status` on the historic run rewrites it at 1.2.0 and main's adapter then 500s the whole workflow list
findings.detail: Resolves the export-bump contradiction as HIGH, agreeing with export-and-compat and not with adapter-server's 'no run broken at merge time'. The status CLI branch calls report(), report() calls export_state(), export_state writes EXPORT_VERSION 1.2.0; main's adapter validates `version: z.literal('1.0.0')`, listRuns wraps projectRun in try/finally with no catch, and projectRun throws invalidRun (500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID). So the first routine status on project-workflows-001 after merge makes the entire project-workflows workflow unlistable, violating the 'existing run must keep loading' criterion. The B PRD does plan a 1.1.0-before-adapter window (pre-run work is ours; server/ is the worker's), so part of this is PRD-designed, but the silent rewrite of the historic run by a read-style command is PR 10's own. Under the score-each-fact-once rule this belongs to export-and-compat; adapter-server for PR 10 should be N/A. Note exportSchema is also a non-strict z.object, so the added review/inputs sections alone would not break anything; only the version literal does.

data.summary: I investigated the aggregation gap rather than re-scoring dimensions: I reconstructed per-PR sums from the verifier means quoted in the gap (the full per-dimension table is not on disk; only the aggregates, PR 9's adapter 0 / ui 1 / export 6 and PR 11's adapter 8.5 / ui 8 are known), read the umbrella and slice PRDs on main to establish which surfaces slice A was told not to touch, and verified in code every fact the disputed scores rest on (adapter version gate, the status-to-export rewrite path, plan-schema strictness, schema provenance, reviewer launch flags). Code quality is PR 11 > PR 10 > PR 9 under every convention I tried (PR 11 8.3, PR 10 between 7.1 and 8.2 depending on its two unknown N/A-surface scores, PR 9 4.9). But once one N/A convention (exclude dimensions where a PR shipped nothing by design) is applied consistently and the two questions are separated with equal weight, "did the better job" most likely flips to PR 10 > PR 11 > PR 9 (about 7.7 vs 7.3 vs 5.5); PR 11 wins that question only if code quality is weighted at 65% or more of "the job". So the gap changes the second answer and PR 9's score (4.4 to 5.5), not the code-quality ranking. Along the way I resolved the export-bump contradiction as HIGH for PR 10 (a routine `workflow status` on the historic run rewrites it at 1.2.0 and main's adapter then 500s the entire workflow list), confirmed PR 9's compat score is earned rather than "by omission", and found that the "PR 11 rewarded twice" concern is arithmetically void under a mean (adding 8.5 and 8 to six dims averaging 8.32 yields 8.30).
data.pr9: Code quality 4.9 (six applicable code dims; adapter-server and ui-and-browser-tests excluded as by-design N/A per docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:17 and docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:5; export-and-compat stays in and is genuinely earned because main's planSchema is a non-strict z.object (server/projects.ts:84) so the new reviewer_transport key is harmless and export_state.py:38 keeps "1.0.0"). Process 6.0. Overall (equal weight) 5.5, up from the raw 4.4, but still last on both questions for a substantive reason, not an N/A artefact: the launch at md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185,219-220 passes `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk` with no `--allowedTools` rule, which PR 10 (handoff line 59-60) and PR 11 (handoff line 54-55) both observed live is denied, so the default native transport cannot produce a verdict; PR 9 skipped the smoke test the PRD makes the merge gate (PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60) and says so honestly (body item 2). Its attach_panels also never adds the third pane (only attach_reviewer_pane does), against work item 3's wording. Cleanest scope discipline and the tightest diff of the three, but a non-working feature.
data.pr10: Code quality between 7.1 and 8.2 depending on the two verifier scores it received for adapter-server and ui (unknown to me; it shipped no server/ or src/ file, so under the exclude convention both drop out and its six real code dims average (50.4 - a - u)/6); my point estimate is 7.4. Process 8.0, the best of the three: it did exactly the slice A the PRDs describe, proved it live twice with artifacts on disk (~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001/ contains review.completion.json, review.json, review.stop.json, review.interactive.json), and its "extra" work is the B PRD's own pre-run list (PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md:11-19). Overall (equal weight) about 7.7. Its one real code defect is HIGH and I verified the mechanism end to end: `workflow status <run>` reaches `print(f"Report: {report(runtime, state)}")` (md-manager-high/workflow/pipeline.py:688), report() calls export_state (479-481), which writes EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0" (export_state.py:16); main's adapter still has `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` with '1.0.0' (server/projects.ts:37,52), listRuns (320-346) has try/finally with no catch, and projectRun throws invalidRun -> 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID (420-421). One status on project-workflows-001 hides the whole workflow list, and the handoff (line 77) understates this as "that run's listing". It is a narrow, fixable defect that the PRD's own plan half-creates, and it is already priced into its export-and-compat score. PR 10 is also the only PR with a single-sourced completion schema (v1.ts -> generated JSON -> completion_schema() at automatic.py:129-131).
data.pr11: Code quality 8.3 (all eight code dims apply; it wrote adapter and UI code and it is good). Process 6.3, dragged by a confirmed high: it implemented B and C directly in one 56-file, +6074 commit after the user had, in the very commit it branched from (61e4752 "Tighten slice A scope and clarify slice ordering"), split the work so that "each run has a smaller, focused diff and a blocked run loses one slice, not all three" (PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:21), and it rewrote the umbrella PRD's status to say so (its own PRD diff). Overall (equal weight) 7.3. The critic's worry that it is "rewarded twice" for the deviation does not survive arithmetic: its other six code dims average 8.32 and adding 8.5 and 8 moves the mean to 8.30, so under a mean the only net effect of the deviation is the spec-fidelity penalty. It is the only PR under which the existing run keeps loading after re-export or `status` (server/projects.ts:44 EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']; test_export.py:185; projects.test.ts:1049), it caught the variadic --add-dir ordering bug (interactive.py:220-226), and it ran four live sessions. Against that, it hand-writes reviewCompletion.schema.json (contracts/workflow/README.md:12 admits "hand-written, not generated from v1.ts"), adds no contract test for it, and duplicates the shape again in Python (automatic.py:129-141), the same triplication contracts-and-schemas faulted PR 9 for.
data.ranking_reason: This is the "did the better job" ranking under one stated rule: exclude a dimension for a PR that shipped nothing on that surface by design (adapter-server and ui for PR 9 and PR 10; export-and-compat stays for everyone), score each fact once (the PR 10 version mismatch lives in export-and-compat only), then average code-quality and process equally. Under that rule PR 10 scores about 7.7, PR 11 7.3 and PR 9 5.5; PR 10 beats PR 11 for any value of its two unknown N/A-surface scores summing below 10.6, which is near-certain given PR 9 received 0 and 1 on the same two dims for the same reason. Substantively: PR 10 did the slice the user scoped hours earlier, proved it live, and its one high (status rewrites the historic run at 1.2.0 and the whole workflow list 500s) is narrow and fixable; PR 11 has the best code and the most complete feature but did a different, larger job than the one specified, in the single big commit the plan was written to avoid; PR 9 is last on both questions because its native reviewer cannot write the completion file and it skipped the gate that would have shown that. The code-quality ranking is different and robust: PR 11 (8.3) > PR 10 (7.1-8.2) > PR 9 (4.9). PR 11 takes "better job" too only if the person weights code quality at 65% or more of the job; the raw 11-dimension means (7.8 / 6.7 / 4.4) hide that flip because they score PR 9 and PR 10 at or near zero on surfaces the PRD told them not to touch.

The umbrella PRD assigns slice A to `workflow/` + `contracts/workflow/` + docs and defers server/ and src/ to feature runs, and the diffstats confirm PR 9 and PR 10 touch neither directory. export-and-compat is different: PR 9's plan.json gains `reviewer_transport`, which is input to the adapter, so the dimension applies and PR 9's 6 is earned (main's planSchema is a non-strict z.object and zod 4.6.5 strips unknown keys; export_state.py stays at 1.0.0). findings.title: Separating 'code quality' from 'better job' with a consistent N/A rule most likely flips the second answer to PR 10
findings.detail: Code-only means with N/A excluded: PR 9 29.4/6 = 4.9; PR 11 66.4/8 = 8.3; PR 10 = (50.4 - a - u)/6 where a,u are its adapter/ui verifier scores (not on disk). PR 11 keeps the code lead unless a+u < 0.5. Process means: 6.0 / 8.0 / 6.3. 'Better job' at equal weight: PR 9 5.45, PR 11 7.32, PR 10 = ((50.4-a-u)/6 + 8)/2, which exceeds PR 11 whenever a+u < 10.6. PR 9 received 0 and 1 on those two dims for the identical reason (nothing shipped there), so PR 10's are almost certainly well under 10.6; at a+u = 6 PR 10 is 7.7. PR 11 wins 'better job' only if code weight w satisfies 8.3w + 6.33(1-w) > 7.4w + 8.0(1-w), i.e. w > 0.65. The raw 11-dim means (7.8/6.7/4.4) hide this because they score two PRs near zero on surfaces the PRD told them not to touch.
findings.evidence: Inputs are the verifier aggregates quoted in the gap: raw 11-dim 4.4/6.7/7.8; code-only 3.8 (4.9 sans N/A)/6.3/8.3; process 6.0/8.0/6.3; PR 9 adapter 0, ui 1, export 6; PR 11 adapter 8.5, ui 8. Reconstructed sums: PR 9 code 30.4, process 18.0; PR 10 code 50.4, process 24.0; PR 11 code 66.4 (six non-adapter/ui dims sum 49.9), process 19.0. No verifier score file exists under the scratchpad (`ls` and `grep -rl verifier` returned only diffs and run copies).

findings.title: `workflow status` on the historic run rewrites it at 1.2.0 and main's adapter then 500s the whole workflow list
findings.detail: Resolves the export-bump contradiction as HIGH, agreeing with export-and-compat and not with adapter-server's 'no run broken at merge time'. The status CLI branch calls report(), report() calls export_state(), export_state writes EXPORT_VERSION 1.2.0; main's adapter validates `version: z.literal('1.0.0')`, listRuns wraps projectRun in try/finally with no catch, and projectRun throws invalidRun (500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID). So the first routine status on project-workflows-001 after merge makes the entire project-workflows workflow unlistable, violating the 'existing run must keep loading' criterion. The B PRD does plan a 1.1.0-before-adapter window (pre-run work is ours; server/ is the worker's), so part of this is PRD-designed, but the silent rewrite of the historic run by a read-style command is PR 10's own. Under the score-each-fact-once rule this belongs to export-and-compat; adapter-server for PR 10 should be N/A. Note exportSchema is also a non-strict z.object, so the added review/inputs sections alone would not break anything; only the version literal does.

findings.title: Only PR 10 single-sources the completion schema; PR 11 deserves the same triplication note PR 9 got
findings.detail: Resolves the fairness contradiction. PR 10 defines reviewCompletion in v1.ts, generates the JSON with contracts:export, and has the Python controller load that JSON for both native validation and print-mode structured output.
